Neither QM5_12582 nor QM5_10505 has any COMPILE_EA-phase work_items row (verified against D:/QM/strategy_farm/state/farm_state.sqlite at registration time), so this registration's 'predecessors' binding is correctly empty for both -- there is no prior compile attempt to supersede.

A plain `enqueue-compile QM5_12582_chan-ng-spring QM5_10505_mql5-macd-sar` (no authority) was attempted first and refused for both EAs: QM5_12582 -> [EX5_ALREADY_PRESENT, WORK_ITEMS_EXIST, BUILD_TASK_EXISTS]; QM5_10505 -> [EX5_ALREADY_PRESENT, EA_ID_REGISTRY_IDENTITY_INVALID, WORK_ITEMS_EXIST, BUILD_TASK_EXISTS, BOUND_SETFILE_HASH_EXISTS]. Both EX5_ALREADY_PRESENT (a build_ea task exists with status=done for each: 8efaa492-33b2-44c0-b87e-6bdc947c154e for QM5_12582, 92f30edc-b19a-4815-a989-251444a9a5d7 for QM5_10505) and WORK_ITEMS_EXIST (both EAs carry dozens of historical Q02 backtest rows, all INFRA_FAIL/INVALID verdicts, no gate PASS) are the expected, correct classifier behavior for an EA that has already been built once and run through Q02 before -- this registration exists to name that the current .ex5/.set state is stale evidence of the pre-instrumentation binary/setfile, not a live compile-fail to repair.

explicitly_not_waived.why_not_waivable: Not a member of compile_work_items.FORCE_REBUILD_WAIVABLE_REASONS; the source-repair/force-rebuild mechanism structurally cannot waive it regardless of this registration.
explicitly_not_waived.diagnosis: framework/registry/ea_id_registry.csv carries two rows for ea_id=10505, both status=active, same slug (mql5-macd-sar) and same strategy_id (b8b5125a-c67f-5bbc-baff-33456e08f5b2), differing only in owner (Research vs Development) and created_at (2026-05-22 vs 2026-06-13). classify_candidate requires exactly one active registry row per ea_id (len(registry_rows) != 1 -> EA_ID_REGISTRY_IDENTITY_INVALID). This is a registry data-hygiene defect (an accidental duplicate row from an ownership handoff, not a magic-number or gate-criteria issue) and is outside this repair's scope -- deduping/retiring one of the two rows is a separate, deliberate registry edit that needs its own review, not a side effect of a compile-authority registration. Diagnosed only; not fixed this cycle. QM5_10505 therefore remains refused (reason: EA_ID_REGISTRY_IDENTITY_INVALID alone) even with this authority applied.
explicitly_not_waived.recommended_follow_up: File a small standalone registry-hygiene ticket to retire the older (2026-05-22, owner=Research) duplicate row for ea_id=10505 with retired_reason=DUPLICATE_ROW, retired_at=<date>, once OWNER/Claude confirms which row is authoritative; then re-attempt this same enqueue-compile with this same authority string.

q02_canary_finding.summary: QM5_12582's governed Q02 canary was NOT dispatched this cycle. farmctl.py enqueue-backtest does not accept Q02 as a manual 'cascade' phase, and --append-only-rerun-of correctly refused (reason q02_append_only_rerun_requires_same_exact_source_and_rerun_row) because the new instrumented compile minted a genuinely new .ex5 identity (33f05561... vs the predecessor row's c6d66c60...), per the standing 23.08 identity rule. The correct tool for a new-identity Q02 successor is farmctl.py requalify-q02 --old-work-item-id ae468d0f-... --expected-current-ex5-sha256 33f05561... --dry-run.
q02_canary_finding.root_cause_of_the_provenance_gap: The current on-disk QM5_12582 XNGUSD.DWX setfile is NOT from this cycle -- it was regenerated on 2026-09-11 by an unrelated, already-committed repair (commit 65e1641235, 'fix(QM5_12582): repair stale Q02 framework wiring', authority router_triage_failure:d9c3f4a8-dbae-4955-ac36-ef0d166f14e0:QM5_12582, evidence docs/ops/evidence/2026-09-11_qm5_12582_stale_framework_rebuild_authority.json) that also changed the .mq5 source (the source this cycle's compile actually used) and removed 9 orphaned qm_filter_* keys / added qm_ea_id -- the same class of hygiene fix as this cycle's QM5_10505 .set fix, done 9 days earlier for QM5_12582 by a different task. Because that 2026-09-11 evidence file has no top-level 'registrations' array, farmctl.py's parameter-change-provenance check (_q02_parameter_change_authority, tools/strategy_farm/farmctl.py ~line 28100) cannot authenticate the parameter diff against it, and this cycle's own new evidence file (this document) was also missing that array at the moment work item 82d760a8 compiled -- compile_evidence.json freezes the exact evidence-file sha256 it saw at compile time, so adding 'registrations' to this document now (see below) cannot retroactively authenticate work item 82d760a8's already-frozen binding. It only helps a future fresh compile made after this edit.
q02_canary_finding.forward_fix_applied_this_cycle: Added a 'registrations' array to this evidence document (schema/shape matching docs/ops/evidence/2026-09-08_qm5_10269_stale_resolver_rebuild_authority.json, the one working precedent found in-repo) and updated both compile_work_items.py BACKLOG_SOURCE_REPAIR_REGISTRATIONS entries' evidence_sha256 to the new file hash. This does NOT retroactively fix work item 82d760a8's frozen binding; it only benefits a future compile made under either authority string after this commit (relevant to QM5_10505 once its registry duplicate is resolved).
q02_canary_finding.recommended_next_step: Either (a) accept QM5_12582's COMPILE_OK as terminal for this cycle and revisit the Q02 canary once a registration path that survives compile-time freezing exists (e.g. a STALE_INCLUDE_CLOSURE_REGISTRATIONS-style mechanism scoped to the specific work_item_id 82d760a8, letting requalify-q02 accept a *current*, not frozen, authority lookup), or (b) if OWNER/Claude judges the parameter diff (9 filter keys removed, qm_ea_id added) genuinely benign and already governed by the 2026-09-11 commit's own authority, extend farmctl.py's provenance check to also accept a registrations entry recorded under a *different*, already-approved authority for the same (ea_id, current source_sha256) -- a deliberate code change, not a blind bypass.
